name: Familial Isolated Hypoparathyroidism Due to Impaired Parathyroid Hormone Secretion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Isolated Hypoparathyroidism

criteria.description: Persistent hypocalcemia with low serum calcium levels
Inappropriately low or undetectable parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels despite hypocalcemia
Exclusion of other causes of hypoparathyroidism such as autoimmune, surgical, or infiltrative etiologies
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting PTH secretion (e.g., PTH gene mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent hypocalcemia with low PTH levels and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes carpopedal spasms and muscle cramps
searchTerms: involuntary muscle contractions due to hypocalcemia

pathognomonic.notes: Facial muscle twitching elicited by tapping facial nerve
Carpal spasm induced by ischemia from blood pressure cuff

common.notes: Generalized tiredness and reduced muscle strength

searchTerms: calcium deposits in brain's basal ganglia
hardening spots in deep brain areas

occasional.notes: Poor enamel formation leading to dental abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including anxiety and depression
occasional.notes: May be related to chronic illness
searchTerms: mood changes including sadness and worry

rare.notes: Due to hypocalcemia affecting cardiac conduction
searchTerms: irregular heart rhythms with long QT

rare.notes: Mild intellectual disability or learning difficulties

laboratory: Hypocalcemia with serum calcium below normal range
Low or undetectable serum intact PTH levels
Hyperphosphatemia due to impaired PTH action
imaging: Basal ganglia calcifications on CT or MRI brain
other: Normal magnesium levels (to exclude hypomagnesemia-induced hypoparathyroidism)
Normal renal function to exclude secondary causes

distinguishingFeatures: History of neck surgery or thyroidectomy
No genetic mutations in PTH gene

redFlags: Severe tetany or laryngospasm requiring emergency intervention
Seizures or altered mental status due to hypocalcemia
